compiled:
📰 General

Hawaii Battles Historic Flooding: Evacuations Ordered Amidst 20-Year Worst Storms •

Catastrophic flooding continues to impact Hawaii as two consecutive storms deliver significant rainfall and strong winds to the islands. Authorities are reporting this is the worst flooding the state has experienced in two decades, causing widespread damage to homes and infrastructure. Residents in affected areas have been ordered to evacuate with officials urging immediate departure due to the dangerous conditions. Road closures and power outages are also being reported across Oahu as emergency services respond to the unfolding crisis.

🌍 World

Israeli Restrictions Fuel Skyrocketing Toy Prices for Eid Celebrations in Gaza •

Residents of Gaza are experiencing difficulties affording toys for Eid al-Adha due to Israeli restrictions on the import of goods. High prices are being driven by limitations on the entry of merchandise into the territory, impacting the purchasing power of many families. Shopkeepers report a significant increase in prices, particularly for popular toys and children’s items. The situation is causing distress for families hoping to celebrate the holiday with traditional gifts for their children.

🦅 US

Iraqi Kurds Celebrate Nowruz, Marking the Persian New Year with Tradition •

The vernal equinox marked the start of Nowruz, a significant holiday celebrated across Iran and in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Traditional Nowruz festivities in Akre involved gatherings and symbolic rituals intended to cleanse the past year and welcome prosperity. The holiday’s observance reflects a blend of Kurdish and Persian cultural heritage, emphasizing family, community, and renewal. Observances included the exchange of gifts and the consumption of traditional foods, signifying hope for a fresh start.

💰 Business

Polymarket’s D.C. Bar Closure Due to Unexpected Power Outage During Opening •

Polymarket’s new bar in Washington, D.C., experienced an abrupt closure shortly after its highly anticipated opening. The bar, designed to host sports betting predictions on over 80 televisions, suffered a power outage that prevented operations. Staff are currently monitoring the situation and assessing the extent of the damage. The outage occurred during the bar’s initial launch, disrupting customer access and planned activities. Authorities are investigating the cause of the power failure.

💻 Technology

Vintage Photos Offer a Nostalgic Glimpse into Life in 1973 •

A collection of 35 photographs provides a visual record of everyday life in 1973. The images depict common scenes from the year, including families traveling in wood-paneled station wagons and children engaging in outdoor play. The photographs showcase prevalent fashion trends, such as wide collars, and highlight the typical leisure activities of the time. The selection offers a tangible representation of a specific era’s cultural and domestic landscape.

🎭 Entertainment

Joseph Duggar Arrested on Child Abuse Charges, Extradition Underway •

Joseph Duggar, a former star of the reality television show “19 Kids and Counting,” was arrested in Tontitown, Arkansas, on Thursday. He is facing a child molestation charge and waived his right to an extradition hearing. This decision initiated his transfer to Florida to await prosecution. Authorities have not yet formally charged Duggar with any offense. The case is currently under investigation.

🏅 Sports

Utah State Aggies Aim for March Madness Upsets, Predict Arizona Score •

Utah State University’s men’s basketball team is participating in the NCAA Tournament for the 26th time, marking their sixth consecutive appearance in the tournament. The Aggies secured a surprising victory over Villanova in the First Four, showcasing their consistent performance in recent years. Head coach Brian Cathon discussed the team’s strategy heading into Friday’s game against Arizona, emphasizing defensive intensity and ball control. The team is seeking to advance to the second round of the tournament, a feat they have rarely achieved.

🔬 Science

Scientists Discover Ancient Microbial Life Deep Beneath Antarctic Ice

Researchers have unearthed evidence of thriving microbial communities in a subglacial lake beneath the West Antarctic Ice Sheet. The discovery, published in Nature, involved drilling through nearly a kilometer of ice to access Mercer Subglacial Lake. Analysis of sediment samples revealed diverse bacterial populations, suggesting a complex and potentially ancient ecosystem. Scientists believe these organisms have been isolated from sunlight and the atmosphere for millions of years, offering a unique window into early life on Earth.

🩺 Health

Newly Identified Virus Found in Humans – Potential for Long-Term Brain Damage •

Scientists have discovered a previously unknown virus, Henipavirus, present in a significant portion of the global population. Estimates suggest the virus infects up to 90% of individuals, residing dormant within cells for their entire lives. Activation of the virus can lead to severe neurological symptoms and, in some cases, brain destruction. Research indicates the virus is related to Nipah virus, known for its high fatality rate in humans. Further investigation is underway to understand the virus’s long-term effects and potential for future outbreaks.
